messages:
alex: Heads up — ran a pos-enc scaling sweep across llama-7b, mixtral-8x, and qwen-7b to check longctx stability. Switching between linear/NTK/YARN variants and toggling head-kv split. Results look ... weird.
mei: summary pls? short bullets ok.
alex: short: (1) mixtral shows a steady perplexity drift starting ~32k tokens for NTK and YARN; linear stays stable but gives higher baseline ppl. (2) latency regression on mixtral NTK at seq_len=65k: p50 up ~1.8x vs linear. (3) observed KV cache growth spikes and occasional stalls during KV flush path.
sam: did you repro on dedicated infra or local dev rigs?
alex: dedicated infra (p4d-reserved), same on 2 different kernel builds (nvcc-13 / 14). perf-ci-bot also ran nightly on dedicated and flagged regressions.
perf-ci-bot: nightly perf-run: model=mixtral-8x variant=ntk seq=65536 p50_latency_ms=234 -> +82% vs baseline (linear=129ms). Regression ticket: #PI-4821
jordan: can you paste the exact runtime config you ran? batching, kernel hints, head/kvdims?
alex: config used (sanitized):
```
model: mixtral-8x
pos_enc: ntk
head_kv_split: true
kv_dim_override: 128
batching: {
  max_batch_tokens: 65536,
  batching_policy: "dynamic", 
  eager_prefill: false
}
kernel_selection: auto
```
mei: kv_dim_override 128 is lower than default, right? might be squeezing kernels into a slower path.
sam: also curious about kernel_selection=auto — did runtime choose small-kernel fallback for certain layers?
alex: yes — profiler shows fallback on attention_kern_v2 for layers 10-12 when seq > 48k. stack trace snippet from perf tracer:
```
[trace] layer=11 attention_kern=attention_kern_v2 fallback=true reason=kv_stride_misaligned
[alloc] kv_cache_expand triggered, alloc_ms=27
[stall] kv_flush_path wait_ms=92
```
jordan: kv_stride_misaligned rings a bell — we changed alignment guarantees in recent head-slice patches. Could be head*kvdim not aligned to 64 bytes.
mei: data point: for llama-7b with same config + ntk we didn't see stalls. So seems model-specific layout interacts with kernels.
sam: what about batching heuristics? dynamic max tokens 65k might create very large per-batch kv allocations — did you try capping max_batch_tokens?
alex: yes, capped to 32k and p50 regressed less (~+20%) and stalls dropped drastically. but perplexity drift persisted for NTK at >32k for mixtral.
perf-ci-bot: nightly-eval: mixtral-8x pos_enc=ntk seq=65536 ppl=4.12 -> baseline linear ppl=3.85 (regression +7%)
mei: regression on ppl is concerning. Could be numerical instability in NTK variant for certain RoPE scale tuning.
jordan: can you run a short perplexity sweep where we keep kv_dim at default, disable head_kv_split, and try pos_enc scale factors +/- 1.0 , 1.2, 0.8? want to decouple head-slicing from pos-enc math.
alex: queued a small run: will report numbers. also instrumented to dump max_abs(attn_scores) per layer.
--- 35 minutes later ---
alex: results: disabling head_kv_split removed the ppl drift for ntk up to 48k, but at 65k still small drift (+2%). max_abs(attn_scores) shows layer 11 had ~3.7x higher magnitude in split-on config.
sam: that suggests head-split changes numeric range which NTK pos-enc amplifies at long ctx. Could explain kernel fallback (overflow guards) and kv flushes.
mei: immediate action items:
- alex: run microbench with head_kv_split off vs on; capture raw fp32 attn matrices and kv cache memory layout (addresses/strides).
- sam: add alignment checks in kernel selector for head*kvdim and emit warnings. If misaligned, try cheap pad to 64 bytes and measure.
- jordan: add an eval job that compares ppl across pos-enc variants for mixtral at 8k/32k/65k and outputs diffs.
alex: ack. I also found a quick mitigation: setting kv_dim_override to 160 (align to 32) reduced fallback occurrences and latency to +10% instead of +82% at 65k. Not a permanent fix but helpful.
jordan: can we backport a runtime patch that enforces 64-byte alignment on GPU allocations? probably low cost.
sam: file a PR for kernel-selector to add an alignment pad option and add a toggle in Dedicated config.
alex: opened PR #rti-1296 with a prototype pad path and a benchmark script.
perf-ci-bot: perf-run rti-1296: mixtral ntk seq=65536 p50_latency_ms=145 (vs 234) — looks promising. full regression suite queued.
mei: thanks. keep the thread updated. if ppl regression persists after kernel changes, we should consider disabling NTK for mixtral on Dedicated by default and add a warning in model catalog.
alex: noted. will follow up with numbers + raw traces. ending here for now. :thumbsup:
